{{Short description|none}}
{{Logical connectives sidebar}}

In [[logic]], a set of [[Symbol (logic)|symbols]] is commonly used to express logical representation. The following table lists many common symbols, together with their name, how they should be read out loud, and the related field of [[mathematics]]. In addition, the subsequent columns contain an informal explanation, a short example, the [[Unicode]] location, the name for use in [[HTML]] documents,<ref>{{cite web|title=Named character references|url=https://www.w3.org/html/wg/drafts/html/master/syntax.html#named-character-references|website=HTML 5.1 Nightly|publisher=W3C|access-date=9 September 2015}}</ref> and the [[LaTeX]] symbol.

== First-order logic ==
{| class="wikitable col1center"
|+ {{sro|Common first-order logic symbols}}
! scope="col" | Symbol
! scope="col" | Unicode<br>value<br>(hexadecimal)
! scope="col" | HTML<br>codes
! scope="col" | [[LaTeX]]<br>symbol
! scope="col" | Logic Name
! scope="col" | Read as
! scope="col" | Category
! scope="col" | Explanation
! scope="col" | Examples
|-
! {{huge|∀}}
| {{mono|U+2200}}
| {{mono|&amp;#8704;}} &amp;forall;
| <math>\forall</math> {{mono|\forall}}
| rowspan="2" | [[universal quantification]]
| rowspan="2" | given any, for all, for every, for each, for any
| rowspan="2" | [[first-order logic]]
| rowspan="2" | <math>\forall x </math>&nbsp;<math>P(x) </math> or<br> <math>(x) </math>&nbsp;<math>P(x) </math> says "given any <math>x </math>, <math>x </math> has property <math>P</math>."
| rowspan="2" | <div style="font-size:90%;"><math>\forall n \isin \mathbb{N}: n^2 \geq n.</math></div>
|-
! {{huge|()}}
|
|
|

|-
! {{huge|∃}}
| {{mono|U+2203}}
| {{mono|&amp;#8707; &amp;exist;}}
| <math>\exists</math> {{mono|\exists}}
| [[existential quantification]]
| there exists, for some
| [[first-order logic]]
| <math>\exists x </math>&nbsp;<math>P(x) </math> says "there exists an <math>x </math> (at least one) such that <math>x</math> has property <math>P</math>."
| <div style="font-size:90%;"><math>\exists n \isin \mathbb{N}:</math> ''n'' is even.</div>

|-
! {{huge|∃!}}
| {{mono|U+2203 U+0021}}
| {{mono|&amp;#8707; &amp;#33;}} &amp;exist;!
| {{mono|<math>\exists !</math>\exists !}}
| [[uniqueness quantification]]
| there exists ''exactly&nbsp;one''
| [[first-order logic|first-order logic (abbreviation)]]
| <math>\exists! x</math> <math>P ( x )</math> says "there exists exactly one <math>x </math> such that <math>x </math> has property <math>P</math>." Only <math>\forall</math> and <math>\exists</math> are part of formal logic.<br> <math>\exists! x</math> <math>P ( x )</math> is an abbreviation for <div style="font-size:86%;"><math>\exists x \forall y(P(y) \leftrightarrow y = x)</math></div>
| <div style="font-size:90%;"><math>\exists! n \isin \mathbb{N}: n+5=2n.</math></div>

|}

| {{mono|<math>\vdash</math> \vdash}}
| [[Logical consequence#Syntactic consequence|syntactic consequence]]
| proves, syntactically entails [[Turnstile (symbol)|(single) turnstile]]
| [[metalanguage|metalanguage (metalogic)]]
| <math>A \vdash B </math> says "<math>B</math> is a theorem of <math>A</math>". In other words,<br> <math>A</math> proves <math>B</math> via a deductive system.
| <div style="font-size:90%;"><math>(A \rightarrow B) \vdash (\lnot B \rightarrow \lnot A) </math><br> (eg. by using [[natural deduction]])</div>

|-
! {{huge|⊨}}
| {{mono|U+22A8}}

| {{mono|<math>\vDash</math>\vDash, \models}}
| [[Logical consequence#Semantic consequence|semantic consequence]] or [[Satisfiability|satisfaction]]
| (semantically) entails or satisfies, models [[double turnstile]]
| [[metalanguage|metalanguage (metalogic)]]
| <math>A \vDash B</math> says<br> "in every [[Structure (mathematical logic)|model]],<br> it is not the case that <math>A</math> is true and <math>B</math> is false".

<math>\mathcal{M}, \sigma \vDash B</math> says<br> a formula

<math>B</math> is true in a model <math>\mathcal{M}</math> with

variable assignment <math>\sigma</math>.
| <div style="font-size:90%;"><math>(A \rightarrow B) \vDash (\lnot B \rightarrow \lnot A) </math><br> (eg. by using [[truth tables]])</div>

|-

| rowspan="3" | [[logical equivalence]]
| rowspan="3" | is logically equivalent to
| rowspan="3" | [[metalanguage|metalanguage (metalogic)]]
| rowspan="3" | It's when <math>A \vDash B</math> and <math>B \vDash A</math>. Whether a symbol means a [[material biconditional]] or a [[logical equivalence]], depends on the author's style.
| rowspan="3" | <div style="font-size:90%;"><math>(A \rightarrow B) \equiv (\lnot A \lor B)</math></div>

| {{mono|U+27DA}}
|
|

|

|U+0305

|[[Overline|combining overline]]
|Used&nbsp;format&nbsp;for&nbsp;denoting [[Gödel numbering|Gödel&nbsp;numbers]]. Using&nbsp;HTML&nbsp;style "4̅" is an abbreviation for the standard&nbsp;numeral "SSSS0".

|U+231C<br>U+231D
|\ulcorner
\urcorner
|top left corner<br>top right corner
|Corner quotes, also called "Quine quotes"; for quasi-quotation, i.e. quoting specific context of unspecified ("variable") expressions;<ref>[[Willard Van Orman Quine|Quine, W.V.]] (1981): ''Mathematical Logic'', §6</ref> also used for denoting [[Gödel number]];<ref>{{citation|last=Hintikka|first=Jaakko|title=The Principles of Mathematics Revisited|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=JHBnE0EQ6VgC&pg=PA113|page=113|year=1998|publisher=Cambridge University Press|isbn=9780521624985}}.</ref> for example "⌜G⌝" denotes the Gödel number of G. (Typographical note: although the quotes appears as a "pair" in unicode (231C and 231D), they are not symmetrical in some fonts. In some fonts (for example Arial) they are only symmetrical in certain sizes. Alternatively the quotes can be rendered as ⌈ and ⌉ (U+2308 and U+2309) or by using a negation symbol and a reversed negation symbol ⌐ ¬ in superscript mode.)
|-

|U+22A9

|forces
|One of this symbol's uses is to mean "truthmakes" in the [[truthmaker theory]] of truth. It is also used to mean "forces" in the set theory method of  [[forcing (mathematics)|forcing]].

|U+22C6

|May sometimes be used for ad-hoc operators.

| box; it is necessary that

| modal operator for "it&nbsp;is&nbsp;necessary&nbsp;that"<br>in [[modal logic|alethic logic]], "it&nbsp;is&nbsp;provable&nbsp;that"<br>in [[provability logic]], "it&nbsp;is&nbsp;obligatory&nbsp;that"<br>in [[deontic logic]], "it&nbsp;is&nbsp;believed&nbsp;that"<br>in [[doxastic logic]],
"it&nbsp;is&nbsp;known&nbsp;that"<br>in [[autoepistemic logic]].
| <div style="font-size:90%;"><math>\Box \forall x P(x)</math> says "it is necessary that everything has property <math>P</math>"</div>

|-
! {{huge|◇}}
| {{mono|U+25C7}}
|
| <math>\Diamond</math> {{mono|\Diamond}}
| [[Modal logic#Modal logics in philosophy|possibility (in a model)]]
| diamond;<br>it is possible that
| [[modal logic]]
| modal operator for "it&nbsp;is&nbsp;possible&nbsp;that", (in most modal logics it is defined as "¬□¬", "it is not necessarily not").
| <div style="font-size:90%;"><math>\Diamond \exists x P(x)</math> says "it is possible that something has property <math>P</math>"</div>
|}
